paper_metadata.title: Influence of Nb, Ta and Ti on microstructure and high-temperature strength of precipitation-hardened Pt-base alloys

evidence.quote: Al was replaced partially by Nb, Ta and Ti in precipitation-hardened Pt-base alloys, resulting in elevated compression strengths at high temperatures.

Pt82Al7Cr6Nb5,P t82Al7Cr6Ta5 and Pt82Al7Cr6Ti5 was investi-gated in a comparative study. Throughout the article, nominal element concentrations are given in at.% by subscript numbers following the element symbol.

parameters.pressure: 5 × 10^4 Pa Ar after evacuation to 10^-3 Pa
parameters.atmosphere: argon, residual oxygen gettered by Ti lump

evidence.quote: The arc-furnace applied for alloy manufacturing was evac-uated to 10−3 Pa and re-ﬁlled with argon to 5 × 104 Pa. The remaining oxygen was trapped by melting a pure Ti lump. Alloy rod ingots of 20 g were then arc-melted in a water-cooled copper hearth, using elements of at least 99.9 wt.% purity. To improve their homogeneity, the rods were re-melted several times
afterwards solution heat treated in a chamber furnace for 6 h at 1500 ◦C and 6 h at 1510 ◦C with subsequent air cooling.
